summary: The last 4 weeks show a highly inconsistent training pattern with very low volume across all three disciplines — swim sessions are short and infrequent, running is sparse with one alarming high-HR effort (179 bpm on July 18th), and cycling has only one meaningful long ride. Sleep quality is severely compromised throughout the period, with multiple nights under 5 hours and body battery readings frequently critically low (as low as 2-5), indicating chronic under-recovery that is significantly limiting training adaptation. Given the nearest target is a marathon in 192 days requiring a sub-4h (5:45/km) pace, immediate focus must be on rebuilding consistent aerobic run volume while first stabilising sleep and recovery.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep above all else — consistently sleeping under 5-6 hours is undermining every training session and increasing injury risk; aim for a strict wind-down routine targeting 7+ hours per night before adding any training load.

Build run frequency before intensity — the July 18th effort at 179 bpm avg HR and 5:02/km pace is far too aggressive for your current base; all running should stay below 155 bpm until you are logging at least 3 runs per week consistently for 3+ weeks.

Increase swim frequency to at least 2 pool sessions per week immediately, as your open-water swim pace (~25-28 min/km) and short distances suggest technique and aerobic swim fitness both need sustained development ahead of the Ironman.

Do not attempt the Wk8 cycling threshold intervals (5x5min @ 210-244W) on August 13th unless Wk6 and Wk7 long rides and sleep averages have both been completed without issue — premature high-intensity cycling will compound accumulated fatigue.

Consider Malta's summer heat (July-August routinely exceeds 35°C) when planning long rides and runs — shift outdoor sessions to before 7am or after 7pm, and factor heat-adjusted pace expectations into all HR-capped efforts.

changes.current_session: Wk6 Evening session: Steady endurance 50-60 min at 128-150W (AI-adjusted down from 128-177W with Z3 blocks)
changes.proposed_session: Skip entirely — take full rest today. Body battery max is 2 (critically low) and sleep data is missing; any training stimulus today will not be absorbed and risks compounding fatigue going into the weekend long sessions.
changes.reason: Body battery of 2 and absent sleep data on July 30th indicate the athlete cannot safely absorb even a reduced Z2 cycling session today.

changes.current_session: Wk6 Long Ride: 84km @ 128-177W (Z2), 240 min, with optional 3x10min Z3 tempo blocks
changes.proposed_session: Reduce to 60-70km @ 128-155W (lower half of Z2 only), cap at 180-200 min, no tempo blocks; stop early if HR climbs above 145 bpm or perceived effort rises above moderate.
changes.reason: Chronic sleep deprivation and near-zero body battery over the preceding days make a full 84km/240-min effort a significant overreach risk this weekend.

changes.current_session: Wk6 Long Run (AI-adjusted): 14-15km @ 6:30-6:45/km, 90-100 min, HR cap 155 bpm
changes.proposed_session: Cap at 10-12km @ 6:45-7:00/km, strictly HR-capped at 150 bpm; walk any uphill sections to keep HR in check. If HR exceeds 150 bpm within the first 3km, convert to a 30-min easy walk and reschedule.
changes.reason: Given the critically low recovery state entering this week and the dangerous HR spike seen on July 18th, a more conservative long run protects against injury and builds a sustainable aerobic base for the marathon target.

changes.current_session: Wk7 Evening session (AI-adjusted): 60 min steady Z2 ride at 128-177W — threshold intervals deferred
changes.proposed_session: Keep as 60 min Z2 at 128-155W (lower Z2 only); this is appropriate given the recovery deficit, but confirm body battery is at least 40+ before starting — if below 40, reduce to 40 min easy spin or skip.
changes.reason: Recovery metrics have been persistently poor and a conditional lower-Z2 ceiling gives a clearer execution rule than an open 128-177W range.

changes.current_session: Wk8 Evening session: Intervals 5x5min @ 210-244W (Z4 Threshold), 3min Z1 recovery, 60-75 min total
changes.proposed_session: Replace with 3x8min @ 178-209W (Z3 Tempo) with 4min easy recovery between, total 55-65 min — only progress to full Z4 threshold work in Wk9 if Wk6 and Wk7 sessions were completed and sleep has averaged 6.5h+ for the preceding 7 days.
changes.reason: Jumping to Z4 threshold intervals in Wk8 without a demonstrated aerobic base and adequate recovery is premature given the last 4 weeks of disrupted sleep and low training consistency.

changes.current_session: Wk8 Long Run: 19.2km @ 6:15-6:45/km, 180 min, with negative-split option
changes.proposed_session: Cap at 16-17km @ 6:30-6:45/km (105-115 min), no negative-split effort; only extend to 19km+ if the Aug 2nd and Aug 9th long runs were both completed without HR exceedances and weekly sleep has improved to 6.5h+ average.
changes.reason: Marathon preparation requires progressive long-run build, but the current recovery deficit means jumping to 19.2km risks overuse injury and sets back training further.
